item.title: Not About the Library
item.description:
Last month, I joined a plenary panel at PALCI's Leading with Impact Conference. Our session was built around a predicament many library leaders know intimately: leading within institutions whose priorities were set without them in the room. Budget pressure, turnover in senior leadership, policy shifts, artificial intelligence, accreditation scrutiny, and enrollment volatility are all recalibrating what campuses treat as urgent. The question is not whether libraries matter to that calculus. It is whether the people doing the calculating know it.

The post Not About the Library appeared first on Ithaka S+R.

item.title: Supporting Veterans as Adult Learners
item.description:
Millions of veterans entered military service with the hope of completing a college education, but have been unable to realize that goal. This disconnect is exacerbated by a range of challenges, including the fact that student veterans disproportionately attend institutions where they are less likely to graduate and, if they do graduate, are likely to see fewer economic benefits. Notably, many veterans receive the GI Bill, which helps pay for education. But it cannot ensure they choose a high-quality program that leads to a credential employers recognize or a career that meets their goals. Supporting veterans requires more than making education affordable.

The post Supporting Veterans as Adult Learners appeared first on Ithaka S+R.

item.title: Keystone Comeback Launches, Helping Adult Learners Return to College Across Southwestern Pennsylvania
item.description:
Thousands of adults across Southwestern Pennsylvania leave college before earning a credential. While many learners want to return, they face financial challenges, competing work and family responsibilities, and difficulty navigating institutional processes. Some also carry an outstanding balance at a school they previously attended, creating another barrier. The Keystone Comeback, a newly launched regional collaboration, will provide such students with the support they need to return to college and finish what they started.

The post Keystone Comeback Launches, Helping Adult Learners Return to College Across Southwestern Pennsylvania appeared first on Ithaka S+R.

item.title: Lessons on Financing the Implementation and Expansion of Comprehensive Student Success Initiatives
item.description:
Over the past few decades, postsecondary institutions have increasingly adopted comprehensive student success interventions designed to address academic, financial, and personal barriers to student persistence and completion. The City University of New York’s Accelerated Study in Academic Programs (CUNY ASAP) is a prominent student success model, replicated across several states, with a substantial body of evidence demonstrating positive outcomes on increasing retention, credit accumulation, graduation rates, and return on investment.

item.title: Will State Law Solve the Library eBook Crisis?
item.description:
Libraries are increasingly facing restrictive eBook licensing terms that can make digital books more expensive, less durable, and harder to preserve than print. In this live discussion, we explore a growing state-by-state movement to establish fairer terms for library eBook contracts—and what these laws could mean for libraries, publishers, authors, and readers. Joining the conversation are Kyle K. Courtney and Juliya Ziskina of the eBook Study Group, and Deborah Schander, State Librarian of Connecticut.

This conversation was recorded on 9/29/2026. Watch the full video recording at: https://archive.org/details/will-state-law-solve-the-library-e-book-crisis

Check out all of the Future Knowledge episodes at https://archive.org/details/future-knowledge

item.title: Digital Preservation Exit Strategy: How to Avoid Vendor Lock-In
item.description:
Digital preservation is a long-term commitment.
